analysis.investment_thesis: Exato Technologies is a small IT-enabled services firm with respectable ROE (28.2%) and a recent profit doubling to INR 10 Cr, but the growth trajectory is decelerating (revenue growth slowed from 56% in FY24 to just 9% in FY25) and the business lacks the proprietary R&D moat I seek. At 35x P/E on a tiny INR 338 Cr micro-cap with rising borrowings and negligible free cash flow, I would wait for more operating history before committing capital.
key_strengths: Strong ROE of 28.2% and ROCE of 26.5% indicate efficient capital deployment at current scale
Operating margin expanded from 8% (FY23) to 11% (FY25); net profit doubled YoY in FY25
Promoter holding solid at 54.73%, suggesting skin in the game
key_risks: Revenue growth collapsed from 56% (FY24) to 9% (FY25) — decelerating growth is my cardinal red flag
Borrowings surged 4.6x in two years (INR 6→28 Cr) while FY25 free cash flow was effectively zero
IT-enabled services is a commoditized space; no evidence of differentiated R&D or proprietary IP
red_flags: Operating CF of -14 Cr in FY24 and FCF of 0 in FY25 despite reported profits
Financing CF of INR 19 Cr in FY25 — growth funded by debt/equity raises, not internal compounding
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my Scuttlebutt lens, Exato fails several of my 15 points. Point 1 (long runway of sales growth) is questionable — the jump from INR 73→114 Cr looked promising, but FY25's deceleration to INR 124 Cr (just 9% growth) suggests either market saturation or lost momentum in its customer-transformation niche. Point 3 (R&D effectiveness relative to size) is unaddressed — the business is described as a "customer transformation partner," which in Indian ITES parlance often means BPO/consulting services rather than innovative product development. Point 5-6 (worthwhile and improving margins) is the one bright spot: operating margins expanded from ~8% to ~11%, and ROE of 28% is genuinely good.

However, the cash flow and balance sheet tell a concerning story that I would want to scuttlebutt aggressively. Borrowings quadrupled from INR 6 Cr to INR 28 Cr while equity only doubled, and FY24 saw a negative INR 14 Cr operating cash flow — a sign of working capital stress common in service businesses chasing growth via receivables. FY25 FCF was zero despite reported profit of INR 10 Cr. At 35x earnings for a micro-cap with a two-year listing history (incorporated 2016, limited public track record), this does not meet my threshold of a "genuinely superior growth company" worth paying a premium for. I would shelve it and revisit after 2-3 more years of operating data.
